Send this round's messages, and say which rows may now be written

mail_round.Rd

The order is the decision: send first, write after. A row whose message did not leave stays as the register has it, so the next round finds it changed again and retries – the queue is the register, and no second state exists to keep aligned. The cost accepted in exchange is a duplicate, never a loss.

Usage

mail_round(
  changed,
  register,
  born,
  mailer,
  dry_run,
  redirect_to = NULL,
  copy_to = NULL,
  reply_to = NULL,
  identified = NULL,
  hosts = NULL,
  granted = character()
)

Arguments

changed

The rows this round would write, from round_changed().

register

The register as read, carrying every field the messages name.

born

The accounts created this round: lists with record_id, upn, credential and created_at, the moment the account was born, from which the welcome and the key count the first sign-in. Without it the two messages leave without the date.

mailer

function(to, cc, subject, body) returning ok and errors.

dry_run

When TRUE nothing is sent and every row comes back writable – the round behaves as it did before this file existed.

redirect_to

One address replacing every recipient, for a field test.

copy_to

Address in copy, on the outcome message only; and the one address the outcome goes to when the row has no established owner.

reply_to

Kept for the caller's symmetry with mail_send(); the mailer closure is what carries it to the transport.

identified

What this round settled about each row, as a frame with record_id and the fields it settled: the identity; composed, the name the round composed, which a collision's message names; owner, who the log says the row belongs to, where the outcome and the key go (mail_referent()); passed, whether the change applied this round handed the row over; edited_by, who changed a held row since it was applied, as the row's log says. register is the register as read, on purpose; this is how the message names what the round has just established rather than what the referent typed.

hosts

Named character vector, instance name to host, as provisioning_reconcile() receives it from the inventory. Only the welcome and the access message read it, to say where the row's instance opens; a row whose instance it does not name gets its message without that address.

granted

The record_ids of the rows whose right this round created and the read-back confirmed: each gets the access message (mail_access_message()).

Value

A list with recapitate, errori and contatori.

Details

The two messages a creation sends are the asymmetry. The account is already born, the round does not create it twice, and the managed identity cannot repair it, so neither the welcome nor the key has a next round. Their failure is not a retry: it is a person's job, and each goes out under its own code, POSTA_BENVENUTO_PERSO and POSTA_CREDENZIALE_PERSA, so an alarm can tell them apart from a message that will simply be retried. They are counted apart from the outcome messages for the same reason, and a welcome that did not leave holds no row back: holding it would not send the welcome again, it would only keep the outcome out of the register.

The access message is the third case of the same asymmetry. It leaves for the rows in granted, whose right this round created and the read-back confirmed, and the right is there whether it leaves or not: the next round finds the row settled and does nothing, so nothing would send it again. Its failure goes out under POSTA_ACCESSO_PERSA, is counted apart in accessi_recapitati and accessi_persi, and holds no row back. It leaves after the welcome, so a person created and granted in the same round reads first that the account exists.

The welcome and the access message go to contact_email, the person, with nobody in copy. The outcome and the key go to the referent, mail_referent(): the owner identified carries. The outcome of a row without one goes to copy_to alone, with a line saying so; its key goes nowhere.
